images.observations: Front perspective personally inspected: original six columns, frames and opaque window backings remain; beige front fascia and bounded recess continuity is coherent, gray terrace/stair supports now connect. Rear perspective personally inspected: broad rear section planes, stepped roofs and unresolved wing ends retain neutral material. Existing section overhang/void below block remains original geometry, not a reconstructed real rear facade.

Front orthographic view personally inspected: six original giant columns and simplified window rhythm intact; no lettering/red-banners invented. Bounded recess/fascia continuity and gray platform are coherent.

Near-front perspective personally inspected: original dark opaque windows and grey-white frames retained; recess edges and front fascia use original warm wall family. Open portico and gray floor/stairs remain distinct.

Left elevation personally inspected: unresolved wing-end and long upper side faces remain neutral; original colored front edges and column retain color. Terrace/stair supports do not color artificial base or broad rear section.

Right elevation personally inspected: original cream column/front pilasters stand against unchanged neutral wing-end and long upper-side supports. Gray front terrace and original stairs are coherent; cut back and base stay neutral.

Top view personally inspected: all roof fields and upper roof cap top remain original neutral. Gray exposed front terrace/stairs follows original model footprint; no roof texture, text or invented features.

Same-camera original-front personally inspected and compared with final front. Original neutral terrace and recess/fascia gaps are the corrected regions; original columns, window backs, frames, proportions and positions remain unchanged.

Same-camera original-rear personally inspected and compared with final rear. Large artificial rear planes, wing section ends and roofs remain neutral and geometrically identical; only front-facing edge/terrace continuity can differ at periphery.
